document.abstract: It may seem presumptious for me to write this plea for a museum, when there are others in the Society who are far better fitted to take up the task, as for instance, Mr. Jenkins, who has made a beginning in this direction by placing in the Smithsonian Institution some of his first apparatus. But as no one else has stepped forward to do so, I have been endeavoring to gather material for the project. I feel as though I were stealing Mr. Jenkins' thunder, but in a measure he has brought this condition about, for it was due to my perusal of his book, Animated Pictures which I purchased in 1897, that I became fired with the ambition to also make Chronophotographic pictures, or in other and more modern language become a “movie” man.
